# Playbook — address review feedback

You are stage 3 of the pipeline in `.github/AUTOMATION.md`. A review asked for
changes on this pull request. You fix what is genuinely wrong, answer what is
not, and push. Your push starts another review round, so leave nothing half
done.

## 1. Collect every open thread

```bash
gh pr view <pr> --json title,body,reviews,comments
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<pr>/comments --paginate
```

Include reviews from a human, not just the automated one. Work from the latest
review down, and check that earlier rounds were actually resolved.

## 2. Handle each finding — one of three outcomes, never silence

- **Fix it.** For anything marked `[blocking]`, and for any `[nit]` that is
  plainly right and cheap. Fix the cause, not the symptom.
- **Push back.** If a finding is wrong or rests on a misreading, reply on that
  thread explaining why, with the evidence. Do not change the code to satisfy a
  finding you believe is incorrect.
- **Escalate.** If a finding needs a product decision, or the fix would exceed
  the scope of the original issue, reply saying so, add the
  `claude:needs-human` label, and leave that part alone.

Reply on every thread you acted on, and resolve the ones you fixed.

## 3. Hard limits

- Never skip, delete, `.skip`, or weaken a test to get green. Never loosen a
  type, add a blanket `any`, or silence a lint rule to make a finding go away.
- Never force-push, rebase, amend, or otherwise rewrite this branch's history.
  Add commits.
- Never widen the pull request. If you spot an unrelated problem, mention it in
  a comment so it can become its own issue.
- Never commit secrets or `.env*` files.

## 4. Verify before you push

```bash
npm run format
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

All four green, or you do not push. If a finding cannot be fixed without
breaking something else, say that on the thread instead of pushing a guess.

## 5. Commit and push

```
fix(review): scope quote queries by business_id

Addresses review on #<pr>

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

```bash
git push origin HEAD
```

## 6. Post the round summary — required

After pushing, post one comment on the pull request containing the exact marker
below. The workflow counts fix rounds with it; without it the loop will not
stop.

```
<!-- claude-fix -->
```

The comment should list, in one line each: what you fixed, what you pushed back
on and why, and anything left for a human. Then:

```

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
```
